ex_en: The glass fell on the floor.
note: pl. أراضي arāDi. على الأرض = on the floor/ground.

phrases.en: he bought a plot of land

ex_en: Open the window, let the air in.
note: Also "wind" in phrases like الهوا قوي.

phrases.en: let's go out for some fresh air

ex_en: They lit a fire to warm up.
note: Feminine. pl. نيران nirān.

ex_en: The house is on top of a small hill.
note: pl. تلال tlāl. Also تل tall.

ex_en: There is an old cave in the mountain.
note: pl. غيران ghīrān. كهف kahf is the formal word.

ex_en: We drove up the sand dune.
note: pl. غرود ghrūd. Saharan word; in the city people often just say كدس رملة or رملة.

phrases.en: the sand dunes in the south

ex_en: Most people live on the coast.
note: pl. سواحل swā7il. In Libya الساحل also names the coastal strip/towns.

ex_en: The Jefara plain has lots of farms.
note: pl. سهول suhūl. Same spelling as the adjective سهل "easy".

ex_en: We sat on a rock by the sea.
note: pl. صخور Skhūr.

phrases.en: there are rocks in the sea

ex_en: My shoes are all mud from the rain.
The house is full of dust after the ghibli.
note: The fine dust on furniture or in the air; تراب is dirt/soil.

phrases.en: there is dust in the air

ex_en: Libya has no river.
note: pl. أنهار anhār. Libya has no permanent river; النهر الصناعي = the Great Man-Made River.

ex_en: The Ubari lakes are in the middle of the sand.
note: pl. بحيرات b7ērāt. Libya's famous ones are the Ubari lakes (بحيرات أوباري).

ex_en: The Derna waterfall is in the Green Mountain.
note: pl. شلالات shallālāt.

ex_en: The Gulf of Sirte is very big.
note: خليج سرت = Gulf of Sirte.

phrases.en: the sea in the bay is calm

ex_en: The boats are tied up in the harbour.
note: Appears in place names (مرسى البريقة). pl. مراسي marāsi.

phrases.en: we went back to the harbour

ex_en: The ocean is bigger than the sea.
note: pl. محيطات mu7īTāt. Also "surroundings".

ex_en: Africa is a big continent.
note: pl. قارات gārāt. In the desert قارة also means an isolated flat-topped hill.

ex_en: The town is on a high plateau.
note: pl. هضاب hDāb.

phrases.en: it's cold up on the plateau

ex_ar: الحمادة كلها حجر ما فيهاش رملة.
ex_en: The hamada is all stone, no sand.
note: Flat rocky desert, as in الحمادة الحمراء (Hamada al-Hamra) in western Libya.

ex_en: We reached the top of the mountain.
note: pl. قمم gimam. Also a "summit" meeting.

ex_en: Next week we'll go out to the countryside.
note: Very Libyan: طلعنا للبر = we went out to the countryside/desert for a picnic or camping trip.

ex_en: The car broke down on us in the middle of nowhere.
note: في الخلا = out in the middle of nowhere.

phrases.en: there's nobody out in the wilds

ex_en: My grandfather lives in the countryside.

phrases.en: from the countryside to the city

ex_en: The view from the mountain top is amazing.
note: pl. مناظر manāDHir.

ex_ar: الشط هذا كله حصى مش رملة.
ex_en: This beach is all pebbles, not sand.
note: Singular حصاية 7Sāya (a pebble).

ex_en: The rain left puddles on the road.
note: pl. برك birak. Different from بركة baraka "blessing".

ex_en: The ring fell to the bottom of the sea.

ex_ar: فيه نسمة باردة جاية من البحر.
ex_tr: fīh nisma bārda jāya min il-ba7ar.
ex_en: There's a cool breeze coming from the sea.
note: Also used for a "soul/person" in counts (عدد النسمات).

ex_en: There's a dark cloud coming.
note: pl. غيوم ghyūm; collective غيم ghēm. سحاب is also used.

ex_en: A strong storm came yesterday.
note: pl. عواصف 3wāSif. عاصفة رملية = sandstorm.

ex_en: The sea is rough, there's a storm.
note: Libyan/Maghrebi word for a spell of stormy, rainy weather.

phrases.en: the fishermen didn't go out because of the storm

ex_en: In the morning the car is covered in dew.
note: Also a girl's name.

phrases.en: the grass is wet with dew

ex_en: It's freezing tonight, dress well.
note: Maghrebi word for biting cold; الدنيا صقع = it's freezing.

ex_en: Hail fell and broke the glass.
note: Maghrebi word; MSA برَد barad.

ex_en: It's not rain, just a bit of drizzle.
After the rain a rainbow appeared.
The flood came down the wadi yesterday.
note: pl. سيول syūl. The wadis fill with sēl after heavy rain.

ex_en: The flood destroyed half the town.
note: pl. فيضانات fayaDānāt. Libyans remember فيضان درنة (Derna flood, 2023).

ex_ar: السنة هذي فيها جفاف، ما صبتش.
ex_tr: is-sana hādhi fīha jafāf, ma Sabbatsh.
ex_en: This year there's a drought, it hasn't rained.
The earthquake happened at night.
note: pl. زلازل zalāzil.

ex_en: Haruj mountain has old volcanoes.
note: pl. براكين barākīn.

phrases.en: like a volcano (about an angry person)

ex_en: Libya's climate is hot and dry.
Did you see the forecast? It'll rain tomorrow.
We go to the sea before sunrise.
note: شروق الشمس.

ex_en: Sunset over the sea is gorgeous.
note: غروب الشمس.

ex_en: The ship appeared on the horizon.
note: pl. آفاق āfāg (also "prospects").

ex_ar: في الصحرا تشوف سراب كأنه مية.
ex_en: In the desert you see a mirage like water.
Tonight the moon is full.
note: Also a man's name. وجهها زي البدر = her face is like the full moon.

phrases.en: the night of the full moon

ex_ar: صار كسوف في الشمس العام اللي فات.
ex_tr: Sār ksūf fish-shams il-3ām illi fāt.
ex_en: There was a solar eclipse last year.
note: Lunar eclipse = خسوف khsūf.

phrases.en: don't look at the eclipse with your bare eyes

ex_en: Tonight there's a lunar eclipse.
note: Solar eclipse = كسوف ksūf.

ex_en: The Earth is a planet, and the sun is a star.
note: pl. كواكب kawākib.

ex_en: My son wants to become an astronaut.
It's dark, turn on the light.
note: الدنيا ضلمة = it's dark.

ex_en: Not a single drop of rain fell.
note: pl. قطرات gaTrāt. Also eye drops (قطرة للعين).

ex_en: Steam is coming out of the pot.
The olive season starts in autumn.
note: pl. مواسم mawāsim. فصل is a season of the year; موسم is a harvest/activity season.

ex_en: There was a fire in the forest.
note: pl. حرايق 7rāyig. نار is fire in general; حريق is a destructive fire.

phrases.en: the fire brigade came to the fire

ex_en: Tea made on embers is tastier.
note: Singular جمرة jamra.

ex_ar: بعد الشوي ما بقى غير الرماد.
ex_tr: ba3d ish-shwi ma bga ghēr ir-rmād.
ex_en: After the barbecue only ash was left.
The lighthouse shines for ships at night.
note: pl. منارات manārāt.

ex_en: Don't swim far, the current is strong.
note: Also electric current (تيار كهربا) and a political "trend".

ex_en: The tide came in and the beach got narrow.
note: المد والجزر = the tides.

ex_en: At low tide the rocks show.
note: Same spelling as جزر jazar "carrots". The Mediterranean tide is small.

ex_en: A big wave came and soaked us.
note: pl. مواج mwāj; collective موج. موجة حر = a heat wave.

ex_en: My brother loves fishing with a rod.
note: صيد الحوت = fishing; صيد الغزال = hunting gazelle.

ex_en: The fishermen are mending the nets.
note: pl. شباك shbāk. Also means a phone/internet network.

ex_ar: شريت صنارة جديدة من سوق الحوت.
ex_tr: shrēt Sannāra jdīda min sūg il-7ūt.
ex_en: I bought a new fishing rod at the fish market.
note: pl. صنانير Sanānīr.

ex_en: Put the bait on the hook.
note: Different from طعم Ta3m "taste".

phrases.en: the fish didn't take the bait

ex_en: We got into a small boat.
note: pl. قوارب gawārib. فلوكة is the usual word for a small fishing boat.

ex_en: The boat went out to sea at dawn.
note: pl. مراكب marākib.

ex_en: The coast guard came in the launch.
note: From English "launch". pl. لنشات lanshāt.

ex_en: The wind pushed the sail.
note: pl. أشرعة ashri3a.

ex_en: Row with the oar to the shore.
note: pl. مجاديف mjādīf.

ex_en: They dropped anchor near the shore.
note: Fishermen also say أنكرة ankra (from Italian ancora).

ex_ar: البنات يلمّوا في الصدف على الشط.
ex_en: The girls are collecting shells on the beach.
note: pl. صدف Sdaf. Same spelling as صدفة "coincidence".

ex_en: Clams are eaten raw with lemon.
note: Collective; one = محارة ma7āra.

ex_ar: الورقة غالية اليوم في سوق الحوت.
ex_tr: il-warga ghālya il-yōm fi sūg il-7ūt.
ex_en: Sea bream is expensive today at the fish market.
note: Libyan fish-market name for dorade/sea bream; same word as ورقة "leaf/paper".

ex_en: Mullet is cheap and eaten in 7rāymi.
Salema is a cheap fish full of bones.
note: Common cheap Mediterranean fish in Libyan markets.

ex_en: There's red coral under the sea.
note: Also the name of a reddish sea bream at the fish market, and a girl's name.

ex_en: Grouper is a big fish with white flesh.
note: Fish-market loanword (Spanish/Italian mero).

ex_en: They said they saw a shark near the beach.
note: Also حوت القرش. Same spelling as قرش "a piece of money".

ex_en: We saw dolphins behind the boat.
note: pl. دلافين dalāfīn.

ex_ar: انتبه، فيه قنديل بحر في المية.
ex_en: Watch out, there's a jellyfish in the water.
note: Also called ميدوزا mēdūza.

ex_en: He brought her a pearl necklace for the wedding.
note: One pearl = لؤلؤة lūlūwa.

ex_en: This door is made of iron.
Gold got very expensive this year.
note: Libyans also say ذهب for gold jewellery in general.

phrases.en: he has a heart of gold

ex_en: This anklet is old Libyan silver.
This tray is pure copper.
note: سوق النحاس / سوق الصياغة in Tripoli old city.

ex_en: We heard gunfire last night.
note: Also bullets; رصاص حي = live rounds.

ex_en: Wrap the fish in tinfoil.
note: Also tinfoil (ورق قصدير).

ex_en: This cup is metal, not plastic.
note: pl. معادن ma3ādin.

ex_en: This table is made of olive wood.
note: pl. أخشاب akhshāb.

ex_en: We gathered firewood to light the fire.
Meat over charcoal comes out tasty.
Libya lives off oil.
note: The formal word; in speech also بترول bitrōl. مؤسسة النفط = the National Oil Corporation.

ex_ar: بابا يخدم في شركة بترول في الصحرا.
ex_tr: bāba yikhdim fi shirkat bitrōl fiS-Sa7ra.
ex_en: Dad works for an oil company in the desert.
note: Everyday synonym of نفط. Petrol for the car is بنزينة banzīna.

ex_en: They shut the oil field because of the troubles.
note: pl. حقول 7gūl. In Libya mostly heard as حقل نفط.

ex_en: The Zawiya refinery is stopped today.
note: مصفاة الزاوية = Zawiya refinery.

ex_en: There's an iron mine in the south.
note: pl. مناجم manājim.

ex_en: They whitewashed the wall with lime.
note: Houses in old Libyan towns were whitewashed with جير.

ex_en: In the old days they coated camels with tar.
note: Traditionally used on camel skin and to waterproof water skins.

ex_ar: ملح البحر أصح من الملح العادي.
ex_tr: mil7 il-ba7ar aSa77 min il-mil7 il-3ādi.
ex_en: Sea salt is healthier than ordinary salt.
note: Libya also harvests salt from sabkhas (salt flats).

ex_en: We spend Friday at my grandfather's farm.
note: Very Libyan word for a family farm or orchard, traditionally irrigated from a well. pl. سواني swāni.

phrases.en: he has a farm in Tajoura

ex_en: The farm has cows and chickens.
note: pl. مزارع mazāri3. Used for bigger or commercial farms; سانية is the homely word.

ex_ar: جدي عاش عمره كله في الفلاحة.
ex_en: My grandfather spent his whole life farming.
note: Everyday word for farm work. أرض فلاحية = farmland.

ex_ar: الزراعة في الجنوب تحتاج مية هلبة.
ex_en: Farming in the south needs a lot of water.
note: وزارة الزراعة = Ministry of Agriculture.

ex_en: The crop is good this year.
note: pl. محاصيل ma7āSīl.

ex_en: The olive harvest this year is huge.
note: Maghrebi word: الصابة باهية = the harvest is good.

ex_ar: الجمعة الجاية جنية الزيتون في السانية.
ex_en: Next week is the olive picking at the farm.
note: جنية الزيتون = the olive harvest, when families gather to pick.

ex_en: The harvest is in summer.
We took the olives to the press.
note: pl. معاصر ma3āSir. Families take their olives to the ma3Sra after picking.

phrases.en: the queue at the olive press

ex_ar: السانية تحتاج ري كل يوم في الصيف.
ex_tr: is-sānya ti7tāj rayy kull yōm fiS-Sēf.
ex_en: The farm needs irrigating every day in summer.
The water runs through the channel to the trees.
note: pl. سواقي swāgi.

ex_en: The kids swim in the irrigation basin.
note: Open masonry basin on a سانية that stores well water for irrigation.

ex_en: The sheep drink from the trough.
note: pl. أحواض a7wāD. Also a sink basin or a fish tank (حوض حوت).

ex_en: The pump is broken, there's no water.
note: From Italian tromba. Also موتور الماء.

ex_en: We installed drip irrigation for the olives.
note: ري بالتنقيط.

ex_en: We put the seeds in the soil.
note: pl. بذور bdhūr. Also زريعة zrī3a for seeds to sow.

ex_en: He bought watermelon seed at the market.
note: Maghrebi collective for seed. (Roasted snack seeds are usually قلوب.)

ex_en: We planted twenty olive saplings.
note: pl. شتلات shatlāt / شتول shtūl.

ex_en: Put fertiliser on the tomatoes so they grow.
note: Also مخصب. Natural manure is زبل zibl.

ex_en: Sheep manure is good for the soil.
note: On the farm it means manure; in town it can also mean rubbish/garbage.

ex_en: In the past they ploughed with a plough and a mule.
note: pl. محاريث m7ārīth.

ex_en: Ploughing comes after the first rain.
note: Verb حرث 7rath, imperfect يحرث yi7rith.

ex_en: Take the hoe and dig around the tree.
note: pl. فيسان fīsān. The basic Libyan farm tool for digging.

ex_en: He reaped the barley with a sickle.
note: pl. مناجل mnājil.

ex_en: He opened the channel with the spade.
note: Used to move earth and open irrigation channels.

ex_en: Olive trees need pruning every year.
They built the pen from palm fronds.
note: One = جريدة jrīda. Used for fences, baskets and roofing.

ex_en: The palm has ten date bunches.
note: pl. عراجين 3arājīn.

ex_en: In the past they made ropes from palm fibre.
note: Palm fibre used for ropes; also a bath scrubber (ليفة līfa).

ex_en: We sat under the grapevine in the courtyard.
note: pl. دوالي dwāli. Many Tripoli courtyards have a dālya for shade.

ex_en: The ears have turned yellow; harvest is near.
note: pl. سنابل snābil.

ex_en: Put out some straw for the animals.
Fodder went up and so did sheep.
note: Price of علف is a big topic for Libyan livestock owners.

ex_en: We planted clover for the cows.
note: Also called فصة fiSSa.

ex_en: Put the sheep back in the pen.
note: pl. زرايب zrāyib.

ex_en: The hens sleep in the coop.
The horses are in the stable.
note: pl. إسطبلات isTablāt.

ex_en: Spring has come and the pasture is good.
note: pl. مراعي marā3i.

ex_en: The kids go out herding with the sheep.
note: Verb رعى ra3a, imperfect يرعى yir3a.

ex_en: He has a big flock of sheep.
note: pl. قطعان giT3ān.

ex_en: This blanket is pure wool.
This wrap is made of camel hair.
Libya imports grain from abroad.
note: Same word means pills/tablets in a health context.

ex_en: The wadi is full of reeds.
note: قصب السكر = sugar cane.

ex_en: Do you have a pet at home?
note: pl. حيوانات أليفة.

ex_en: My grandfather has livestock on the farm.
note: Singular بهيمة bhīma. Used as an insult too (يا بهيمة = you dumb animal).

ex_en: Livestock prices are rising before Eid.
note: Formal/news word; at home people say بهايم or غنم.

ex_en: My uncle works in beekeeping.
note: تربية الدجاج = poultry farming; in people, "upbringing/manners".

ex_en: Put the saddle on the horse.
note: pl. سروج srūj. The decorated Libyan saddle is used at fantasia shows.

ex_en: He pulled the reins and the horse stopped.
The bird in the cage is singing.
note: pl. أقفاص agfāS. Also a crate of fruit/veg.

ex_en: We set a trap for the mouse.
note: pl. فخاخ fkhākh. Also figuratively: طاح في الفخ = he fell into the trap.

ex_en: There's a pigeon nest above the window.
note: pl. عشوش 3shūsh.

ex_ar: عنده عشر خلايا نحل في الجبل.
ex_en: He has ten beehives in the mountains.
note: pl. خلايا khalāya. Also a (biological or militant) cell.

ex_en: The cow gave birth to a calf yesterday.
note: pl. عجول 3jūl. Also لحم عجل = veal.

ex_en: This bull is very strong.
note: pl. ثيران thīrān.

ex_en: The goat had two kids.
note: pl. جديان jidyān. Same spelling as جدي jiddi "serious".

ex_en: The billy goat has long horns.
note: pl. تيوس tyūs. Also an insult for a stubborn person.

phrases.en: a billy goat and ten nanny goats

ex_en: We bought a lamb for Eid.
note: pl. خرفان khirfān. In Libya علوش is the common word; خروف is pan-Arabic.

ex_en: This year we bought a fat yearling sheep.
note: A sheep in its second year, the preferred age for the Eid sacrifice. Same word as the حولي wrap (clothing).

ex_en: The mare had a white foal.
note: Female مهرة muhra. Not the same as مهر mahr "dowry".

phrases.en: the foal runs after its mother

ex_en: The ducks swim in the pond.
note: Collective بط baTT.

ex_ar: الوز يصيّح لو يجي حد غريب.
ex_en: The geese honk if a stranger comes.
note: Collective وز wizz.

ex_en: We bought a turkey for the dinner party.
The hen hatched ten chicks.
note: pl. فراخ frākh. Also used for the young of other animals.

ex_ar: عنده مية راس بل في الجنوب.
ex_en: He has a hundred head of camels in the south.
note: Libyans say البل il-bil. Singular جمل/ناقة.

ex_en: There are wild boars in the forest.
note: Maghrebi word; MSA خنزير khanzīr. Also a strong insult.

ex_en: Muslims don't eat pork.
note: pl. خنازير khanāzīr. Everyday Libyan also حلّوف.

ex_en: We saw a bear at the zoo.
note: pl. دببة dibaba.

ex_en: Is the tiger faster than the lion?
note: pl. نمور nmūr.

ex_en: The kids love to see the elephant.
note: pl. فيلة fiyala / فيلان fīlān.

ex_en: The monkey is eating bananas.
note: pl. قرود grūd. Also a playful insult for a naughty child.

ex_en: The giraffe has a long neck.
The fox ate the hen.
note: pl. ثعالب tha3ālib. Also a cunning person.

ex_ar: زمان يقولوا فيه ضباع في الجبل.
ex_en: In the past they said there were hyenas in the mountains.
note: pl. ضباع Dbā3.

ex_en: We found a hedgehog on the farm.
note: Maghrebi form; MSA قنفذ.

phrases.en: the hedgehog rolls into a ball

ex_en: The Barbary sheep lives in the desert mountains.
note: Wild mountain sheep of the Libyan Sahara; a symbol of the town of Waddan and of Libyan wildlife.

ex_en: The jerboa hops like a kangaroo.
note: pl. يرابيع yarābī3. Small hopping desert rodent.

ex_ar: الصغير يخاف من الوحوش في الليل.
ex_en: The little one is scared of monsters at night.
note: pl. وحوش w7ūsh. Slang: وحش = a beast (impressive person/thing).

ex_en: The dab lizard lives in the desert.
note: Large desert lizard; some Bedouin eat it.

ex_en: The monitor lizard is almost a metre long.
note: pl. ورلان warlān.

ex_ar: فيه بوبريص على الحيط في الكوجينة.
ex_en: There's a gecko on the kitchen wall.
note: From أبو بريص. The little gecko seen on walls at night.

ex_en: The lizard ran between the stones.
note: Maghrebi word for the small ground lizard. MSA سحلية.

ex_en: The chameleon changes its colour.
note: Also figuratively a two-faced person.

ex_en: The crocodile lives in the Nile.
note: pl. تماسيح tamāsī7.

ex_ar: الجران يغنوا في الليل في الساقية.
ex_en: The frogs croak at night in the channel.
note: Maghrebi word; MSA ضفدع Dafda3. pl. جران jrān.

ex_en: Careful, there's a viper under the stone.
note: Libyan/Maghrebi form of أفعى; حنش is a snake in general.

ex_en: Bats come out at night.
note: pl. خفافيش khafāfīsh.

ex_en: The owl hoots at night.
note: Seen as a bad omen by some people.

ex_en: The eagle is flying above the mountain.
note: pl. نسور nsūr.

ex_en: The falcon caught a pigeon.
note: pl. صقور Sgūr. Falconry (الصيد بالصقور) is practised in the Libyan desert.

ex_en: The crow is standing on the pole.
note: pl. غربان ghirbān. Considered a bad omen.

ex_en: The birds sing early in the morning.
note: pl. عصافير 3aSāfīr.

phrases.en: killed two birds with one stone

ex_en: The starlings came with the winter.
note: pl. زرازير zarāzīr. Large flocks come in winter.

ex_en: They hunted partridges in the mountains.
note: pl. حجل 7jal.

phrases.en: she walks gracefully like a partridge

ex_en: The quail come in autumn.
note: Migrating quail pass the Libyan coast in autumn.

ex_en: The turtle dove built a nest in the vine.
note: pl. يمام ymām.

ex_en: The parrot can say hello.
note: Also used for someone who repeats without understanding.

ex_en: The ostrich egg is very big.
note: pl. نعام n3ām.

phrases.en: like an ostrich (head in the sand)

ex_en: Our neighbour has a canary that sings.
Seagulls are flying over the port.
note: pl. نوارس nawāris.

ex_en: The nightingale sings in the tree.
note: Also said of someone who speaks a language fluently (يتكلم زي البلبل).

ex_en: I saw a hoopoe on the farm.
note: Known from the Quran story of Solomon.

ex_en: The peacock spread its feathers.
note: Also said of a vain person.

ex_en: The houbara comes to the desert in winter.
note: Desert bird hunted with falcons.

ex_en: The saluki runs faster than a hare.
note: Lean hunting dog of the Bedouin.

ex_en: The dog had five puppies.
note: Also a harsh insult for a woman.

ex_en: The cat had little kittens.
note: Masc. قطوس gaTTūs.

ex_en: The buffalo gives a lot of milk.
note: Collective جاموس jāmūs.

ex_en: The zebra is striped black and white.
The cheetah is the fastest animal.
note: Also a man's name.

ex_en: The squirrel climbed up the tree.

ex_ar: الحوت الكبير أكبر حيوان في الدنيا.
ex_en: The whale is the biggest animal in the world.
note: Since حوت alone means "fish" in Libya, a whale is حوت كبير or حوت أزرق.

ex_en: The sea turtle lays eggs in the sand.
note: Loggerhead turtles nest on Libyan beaches. On land, a tortoise is فكرون.

ex_en: Wildlife has become scarce in Libya.
note: برّي = wild (vs. tame/domestic).

ex_en: We took the kids to the zoo.
note: Tripoli zoo is in أبو سليم.

ex_en: The house is full of insects in summer.
note: pl. حشرات 7asharāt.

ex_en: The butterflies in spring are colourful.
note: pl. فراشات farāshāt.

ex_en: The locusts ate all the crops.
note: Collective جراد jrād. Locust swarms sometimes hit southern Libya.

ex_en: The dog has fleas.
note: pl. براغيث barāghīth.

ex_en: She brought lice home from school.
note: Collective قمل gmal. Lice in school kids' hair is a common worry.

ex_en: There's a spider in the corner of the room.
note: pl. عناكب 3anākib.

ex_en: The apple has a worm in it.
note: Collective دود dūd.

ex_en: The hotel had bedbugs.
note: Collective بق bagg.

ex_en: A wasp stung me on the hand.
note: pl. دبابير dbābīr.

ex_en: A black beetle is walking on the floor.
note: pl. خنافس khnāfis.

ex_en: After the rain the snails came out.
note: After rain the snails come out on the farm.

phrases.en: he moves at a snail's pace

ex_en: A tick got stuck on the dog.
note: Collective قراد grād.

ex_en: The caterpillar becomes a butterfly.
note: pl. يرقات yargāt.

ex_en: The pillow is stuffed with feathers.
note: One = ريشة rīsha (also a pen nib or paintbrush). Same word means lamb chops at the butcher's.

ex_en: The bird's wing is broken.
note: pl. جوانح jwāni7 (also chicken wings as food) / أجنحة.

ex_en: The bird pecked with its beak.
note: pl. مناقير mnāgīr.

ex_en: The dog is wagging its tail.
note: pl. ذيول dhyūl. Also the tail end of something.

phrases.en: at the bottom of the list

ex_en: This ram has big horns.
note: pl. قرون grūn. Same spelling as قرن garn "century".

ex_en: The horse needs a shoe on its hoof.
note: pl. حوافر 7wāfir.

ex_en: The camel stores fat in its hump.
The elephant drinks with its trunk.
note: pl. خراطيم khrāTīm. The same word is used for a water hose.

ex_en: The cat scratched me with its claws.
note: pl. مخالب mkhālib.

ex_en: The mouse went into its hole.
note: pl. جحور j7ūr.

phrases.en: he never leaves his den (a homebody)

ex_en: A flock of pigeons is flying over the city.
note: pl. أسراب asrāb.

ex_en: I couldn't sleep because of the dogs barking.

ex_ar: الكلب ينبح على كل واحد يفوت.
ex_en: The dog barks at everyone passing by.
note: imperfect: ينبح yinba7. Proverb: الكلب اللي ينبح ما يعضش.

ex_en: The donkey's braying woke us up in the morning.
note: Verb نهق nhag, imperfect ينهق yinhag.

phrases.en: his voice is like a braying donkey

ex_en: I love the birds chirping in the morning.
note: Verb زقزق zagzag, imperfect يزقزق yzagzig.

ex_en: The jackal howls at night.
note: imperfect: يعوي y3awi. Noun عواء 3uwā.

ex_en: We heard the horses neighing from afar.
note: Verb صهل Sahal.

ex_en: We got up at cockcrow.
note: Verb: الديك صاح / يصيّح.

ex_en: My uncle loves horses.
note: Singular حصان / فرس. Horse culture: الفروسية and fantasia shows.

ex_en: The lioness hunts for the lion.
The cub plays with its mother.
note: pl. أشبال ashbāl. Also junior sports teams (الأشبال).

ex_en: The leaves fell in autumn.
note: pl. ورق warg (collective) / أوراق awrāg. Same word as "sheet of paper".

ex_en: The wind broke a branch off the tree.
note: pl. أغصان aghSān. Also فرع far3.

ex_en: The tree's roots cracked the wall.
note: pl. جذور jdhūr. Libyans also say عروق 3rūg for roots.

ex_ar: جذع الزيتونة هذي عمره مية عام.
ex_en: This olive trunk is a hundred years old.
note: pl. جذوع jdhū3.

ex_en: Prickly pears have thorns, be careful.
note: One = شوكة shōka (also a fork). Fish bones are also شوك.

ex_ar: الربيع جا والنوّار طالع في البر.
ex_en: Spring has come and flowers are out in the countryside.
note: Maghrebi collective for flowers/blossom; one = نوّارة nuwwāra.

ex_en: The scent of jasmine fills the house.
note: Also a girl's name.

ex_en: He bought a bunch of jasmine from the vendor.
note: Much loved in Libya: men wear a sprig of فل behind the ear, and it is sold in small bunches (مشموم) in summer.

ex_en: The night jasmine releases its scent after sunset.
note: Courtyard shrub whose scent fills summer nights.

ex_en: Narcissus blooms at the end of winter.
note: Also a girl's name.

ex_en: We planted sunflowers by the wall.
note: The roasted seeds are sold as قلوب.

ex_en: My mother fumigates the house with harmal.
note: Desert plant whose seeds are burned as incense against the evil eye.

ex_ar: حط شوية شيح في الشاهي للكرشة.
ex_en: Put a little wormwood in the tea for your stomach.
note: Bitter desert herb; added to tea and used as a folk remedy.

ex_en: My grandmother weaves baskets from esparto.
note: Tough grass used to weave mats, baskets and ropes; once a major Libyan export.

ex_en: The wadi is full of broom bushes.
note: Common shrub of Libyan wadis; used as firewood and fodder.

ex_ar: قعدنا في ظل طلحة في الصحرا.
ex_en: We sat in the shade of an acacia in the desert.
note: Thorny acacia of the southern desert; one = طلحة Tal7a.

ex_en: Sidr honey is very expensive.
note: Its leaves are traditionally used to wash the dead and as a hair rinse; its honey (عسل السدر) is prized.

ex_ar: زرعوا الأثل حول السانية يصد الريح.
ex_en: They planted tamarisk round the farm to block the wind.
note: Hardy tree planted as windbreaks in oases and along roads.

ex_en: Juniper is common in the Green Mountain.
note: Grows in the Green Mountain (الجبل الأخضر).

ex_en: Carob syrup is tasty with 3aSīda.
note: The tree and its pods; carob syrup (رب الخروب) is a Libyan favourite.

ex_ar: فيه شجر بطوم قديم في الجبل.
ex_en: There are old terebinth trees in the mountains.
note: Tree of the Libyan hills; its small fruits were eaten and pressed for oil.

ex_en: Oak trees live a hundred years.
The pine forest is near the sea.
note: Also the pine nuts used in sweets.

ex_en: Cypress trees are tall and slender.

phrases.en: tall and slim as a cypress

ex_en: The road is lined with eucalyptus trees.
note: Planted along Libyan roads in the Italian era; leaves boiled for colds.

ex_en: The farm is fenced with cactus.
note: Prickly-pear hedges are a familiar sight around farms.

ex_ar: أمي عندها طاسة حبق في الحوش.
ex_en: My mother has a pot of basil in the courtyard.
note: Maghrebi word for sweet basil, often grown in a pot by the door.

ex_en: Oleander is pretty but poisonous.
note: Common ornamental shrub in Libyan streets and wadis; poisonous.

ex_en: Plants need sun and water.
note: pl. نباتات nabātāt. One plant: نبتة nabta.

ex_ar: الشجرة هذي ما عطتش ثمار العام هذا.
ex_tr: ish-shajra hādhi ma 3aTatsh thmār il-3ām hādha.
ex_en: This tree didn't bear fruit this year.
note: pl. ثمار thmār. Also figurative: ثمرة التعب = the fruit of hard work.

ex_en: My grandmother treats people with herbs.
note: Singular عشبة. Also herbal remedies sold by the 3aTTār.

ex_en: The camel is eating hay.
note: One straw: قشة gashsha. القشة اللي قصمت ظهر البعير = the last straw.

phrases.en: the straw that broke the camel's back

ex_en: Take a stick and poke the fire.
note: pl. أعواد a3wād / عيدان 3īdān. Also oud (incense wood) and the lute.

ex_en: He has an orange orchard on the coast.
note: pl. بساتين basātīn. In Libya سانية is more common.

ex_en: I brought her a bouquet of flowers.
note: pl. زهور zhūr. More formal than وردة / نوّار; also a girl's name and the planet Venus.

ex_en: Violets have a delicate scent.
note: The colour is بنفسجي.

ex_en: We planted small bushes in front of the house.
note: Diminutive of شجرة. pl. شجيرات.

ex_en: The trees on this street are old.
note: Collective of شجرة; pl. أشجار ashjār.
